source_text: XIII. Ἀκούω δὲ ὅτι καί τινας ὑμῶν Ἰουδαῖοι καλοῦσιν εἰς συναγωγάς· διὸ προσέχετε μή ποτε ὑμῶν καὶ μεῖζον καὶ ἑκούσιον ἁμάρτημα ἅψηται, μηδέ τις τὴν ἀναφαίρετον ἁμαρτίαν τὴν εἰς τὴν βλασφημίαν τοῦ ἁγίου πνεύματος ἁμαρτήσῃ. Μὴ γίνεσθε ἅμα αὐτοῖς ἄρχοντες Σοδόμων καὶ λαὸς Γομόρρας, ὧν αἱ χεῖρες αἵματος πλήρεις. Ἡμεῖς δὲ οὔτε προφήτας ἀπεκτείναμεν οὔτε τὸν Χριστὸν παρεδώκαμεν καὶ ἐσταυρώσαμεν. Καὶ τί πολλὰ λέγω ὑμῖν; Μνημονεύετε ὧν ἠκούσατε (καὶ νῦν περαίνετε ἃ ἐμάθετε). Ἐπεὶ κἀκεῖνο ἠκούσατε ὅτι φασὶν οἱ Ἰουδαῖοι· Ὁ Χριστὸς ἄνθρωπος ἦν καὶ ἀνεπαύσατο ὡς βιοθανής. Εἰπάτωσαν οὖν ἡμῖν, ποίου βιοθανοῦς πᾶς ὁ κόσμος μαθητῶν ἐπληρώθη; Ποίου βιοθανοῦς ἀνθρώπου οἱ μαθηταὶ καὶ ἄλλοι μετ᾽ αὐτοὺς τοσοῦτον ὑπὲρ τοῦ ὀνόματος τοῦ διδασκάλου αὐτῶν ἀπέθανον; Ποίου βιοθανοῦς ἀνθρώπου τῷ ὀνόματι τοσούτοις ἔτεσι δαιμόνια ἐξεβλήθη καὶ ἐκβάλλεται καὶ ἐκβληθήσεται; Καὶ ὅσα ἄλλα μεγαλεῖα ἐν τῇ ἐκκλησίᾳ τῇ καθολικῇ γίνεται. Ἀγνοοῦσι δὲ ὅτι βιοθανής ἐστιν ὁ ἰδίᾳ προαιρέσει ἐξάγων ἑαυτὸν τοῦ βίου. Λέγουσι δὲ καὶ νεκυομαντείαν πεποιηκέναι καὶ [ἀνηγειοχέναι — verb unreadable in scan; sense from context: raised/brought up, the resurrection charged as sorcery] τὸν Χριστὸν μετὰ τοῦ σταυροῦ. Καὶ ποία γραφὴ τῶν παρ᾽ αὐτοῖς καὶ παρ᾽ ἡμῖν ταῦτα περὶ Χριστοῦ λέγει; Τίς δὲ τῶν δικαίων ποτὲ εἶπεν; Οὐχ οἱ λέγοντες ἄνομοι εἰσί; Πῶς δὲ ἀνόμοις λέγουσι πιστεύσῃ τις, καὶ οὐχὶ τοῖς δικαίοις μᾶλλον;
pass_a_gloss: I hear that Jews are also calling some of you into synagogues; therefore be on guard lest a still greater and willful sin seize hold of you, and lest anyone commit the unremovable sin that is unto blasphemy of the Holy Spirit. Do not become together with them rulers of Sodom and people of Gomorrah, whose hands are full of blood. We for our part neither murdered prophets nor handed over and crucified Christ. And why do I say many things to you? Remember what you heard, and now bring to completion what you learned. For you also heard this, that the Jews say: Christ was a man and came to rest as one dead untimely. Let them then tell us: of what untimely-dead man was the whole world filled with disciples? Of what untimely-dead man did the disciples and others after them die so greatly for the name of their teacher? By the name of what untimely-dead man through so many years have demons been cast out and are being cast out and will be cast out? And however many other mighty works happen in the catholic church. But they do not know that untimely-dead is the one who by his own deliberate choice leads himself out of life. And they say that Christ both practiced calling up the dead and, after the cross, did the raising act charged as sorcery. And what scripture, whether among them or among us, says these things about Christ? Which of the righteous ever said it? Are not those who say them lawless? How would anyone trust the sayings of lawless men, and not rather the righteous?
pass_b_english: I hear that the Jews are calling some of you also into their synagogues, so be watchful, lest an even greater and willful sin fasten upon you, and lest any of you commit the sin that cannot be taken away, the sin unto blasphemy of the Holy Spirit (Matthew 12:31). Do not become with them rulers of Sodom and people of Gomorrah (Isaiah 1:10), whose hands are full of blood (Isaiah 1:15). We, for our part, neither murdered the prophets nor betrayed and crucified the Christ. Why should I speak many words to you? Remember what you have heard, and now carry through to the end what you have learned.

For you have heard this too, that the Jews say Christ was merely a man and died an untimely death. Let them tell us, then: of what man dead before his time has the whole world been filled with disciples? Of what man dead before his time did the disciples, and others after them, die so great a death for their own teacher's name? By the name of what man dead before his time, through so many years, have demons been cast out and are still cast out and shall be cast out, with all the other mighty works that come to pass in the catholic church? Yet they do not know that one dead before his time is the one who by his own deliberate choice carries himself out of life. They even say that Christ worked necromancy and by that art wrought a raising after the cross [verb lost — the charge being resurrection-sorcery]. What scripture, whether theirs or ours, says such things about Christ? What righteous man ever said it? Are not those who say it lawless men? How could anyone put trust in the words of the lawless rather than in the righteous?
